rawOutput.rationale: Start with a compact causal map, then move through the outbreak sequence and end with a simple 1914 to 1918 timeline. This matches the learner's need for a big picture first and supports later sessions on widening the war.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions made a regional crisis likely to spread.
The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, which moved from ultimatum to mobilization and declarations of war.
World War I runs from 1914 outbreak through 1918 armistice, with 1917 as a major turning point.

Classify each key item as cause, event, or consequence.

methodBriefing.what: Study a compact model, explain it in your own words, repair what is missing, then explain it again.

how: Say the idea back in plain language.

activities.label: Big picture map
activities.title: A Europe ready to widen
activities.body: Build the first map. Focus on the broad causes and one concrete example.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions made a regional crisis likely to spread.

activities.label: Your first explanation
activities.title: Explain the outbreak chain
activities.body: Say the chain in your own words. Keep it to causes and the next step.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination led to the July Crisis, then ultimata, mobilization, and declarations of war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the assassination, the crisis, and the move into war. If needed, repair by keeping the steps in order.

activities.label: Fix the sequence
activities.title: Repair the war start sequence
activities.body: Use the hint to correct the order. Give a tighter version than before.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The assassination itself was the war, so the later crisis steps do not matter.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination was the trigger, not the war itself; the July Crisis, mobilization, and declarations of war came next.
activities.feedback: The key repair is that the assassination triggered a chain of events. The missing step is the July Crisis leading into war declarations.

activities.label: Timeline from memory
activities.title: Retell 1914 to 1918
activities.body: Retell the timeline from start to finish. Include the turning point year.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I begins in 1914, the war continues through 1917 as a major turning point, and ends with the 1918 armistice.
activities.feedback: A complete answer anchors the start, a middle turning point, and the end. If you missed one, place it on the line from 1914 to 1918.

activities.label: Quick check
activities.title: Which event came first?
activities.body: Choose the first event in the outbreak chain.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
choices: The U.S. entry into the war
activities.feedback: The assassination came first and set the July Crisis in motion. The other choices happened later.

activities.label: Return point
activities.title: Pause and return later
activities.body: Name one idea you want to keep active for next time. Then stop here.

activities.label: Learn
activities.title: Rival blocs before 1914
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs before 1914.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: Rival blocs before 1914
activities.body: How did prewar European alliances shape tensions before 1914?
activities.concept: Prewar European alliances and tensions split Europe into rival blocs before 1914.
activities.correctAnswer: They divided Europe into rival alliance blocs, which increased suspicion and made a wider war more likely.
activities.feedback: The key link is that alliances hardened divisions and raised the risk of escalation.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: From assassination to war
activities.body: What sequence followed the Sarajevo assassination before wider war began?
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia and then war
activities.correctAnswer: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, then declared war after tensions escalated.
activities.feedback: The crisis moved from assassination to ultimatum, then to declaration of war.

activities.label: Explain
activities.title: World War I dates
activities.body: What is the basic chronology of World War I from 1914 to 1918?
activities.concept: Basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 places World War I between those years.
activities.correctAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918.
activities.feedback: The correct frame is the war's start and end years.
